implementation.improvement: Caches only recent healthy low-pressure telemetry for a bounded interval so successive flushes can reuse it without another pressure query. The cache is invalidated on pressure, loss, failed or successful submission, explicit acknowledgement, and resynchronization re-query.
implementation.safety: The cache is advisory and never replaces kernel batch admission. FULL/LOSS/EAGAIN states invalidate it; stale or unavailable monotonic time disables cache reuse and falls back to a fresh query.
implementation.bounds: Cache duration is configurable up to 100 ms and defaults to 1 ms. Configuration rejects values above the cap. The implementation uses monotonic timestamp expiry and no unbounded state.
implementation.security: No capability, lineage, tenant, telemetry, or model-authority boundary is bypassed; the optimization only avoids redundant userspace queries between validated healthy observations.

productivity_interpretation.benefit: In the controlled unit scenario, pressure queries fell from 16 in the M159 behavior to 14 with two cache hits while flush, loss, resynchronization, and fast-rejection behavior remained covered.
productivity_interpretation.scope: This is a measured control-path query reduction, not a claim of universal workload speedup or reduced kernel execution time on physical accelerators.
productivity_interpretation.raw_throughput_scope: The integrated gate retained the inherited M155 synthetic QEMU accounting benchmark at speedup_x100=95 in this run; M160 does not claim an isolated raw-throughput gain.

build_artifact.kernel_source: M156 kernel image reused; M160 is userspace runtime/test integration.

release_gate.reason: M160 is bounded userspace/QEMU validation. Physical accelerator qualification, independent reproducible production builders, signed artifacts, stable/LTS forward-port qualification, and external security governance remain required.
release_gate.hardware_claim: No physical GPU, NPU, VRAM, IOMMU, DMA, vendor-driver, reset, or fleet qualification is claimed.

known_limitations: The cache is useful only for healthy low-pressure state and is deliberately invalidated whenever the safety state may have changed.
The two-query reduction is from a deterministic unit scenario compared with the immediately previous M159 state machine, not a fleet-wide benchmark.
The unit test uses an injected ioctl model; QEMU validates integration and packaging, not physical accelerator behavior.
No isolated M160 raw-throughput improvement is claimed; the M155 benchmark remains supporting context only.
The kernel remains based on the Linux v7.2-rc7 development line and production release qualification remains incomplete.
